description: The Descent Sieve leverages the fact that if T^k(n_0) < n_0 for any residue class representative n_0, then T^k(n) < n for ALL n sharing the same k least significant bits (Theorem 2.5, Angeltveit 2026). This ratio-based pruning eliminates entire exponentially-sized families of integers from a single comparison, analogous to dominance pruning in scheduling theory.
mathematical_formalization: If n_1 = n_0 + a * 2^k and T^k(n_0) < n_0, then T^k(n_1)/n_1 <= T^k(n_0)/n_0 < 1, hence T^k(n_1) < n_1. The proof uses the monotonicity of T(m)/m = 3/(2(1 + 1/(3m))) for odd m.
analogical_connections: Dominance pruning in single-machine scheduling — if job A dominates B in all extensions, prune B
Alpha-beta pruning in game trees — a position proved losing for all continuations need not be explored
Coarsening in multigrid methods — prove convergence at coarse scale, inherit at fine scale
implementation_hypothesis: At each recursion level k in the bit-tree, compute ratio_k = T^k(n_0) / n_0 using fixed-point arithmetic. If ratio_k < 1.0, prune. Track ratio bounds through the recursion to enable speculative pruning.
experiment_seed: For N=40..60, measure the fraction of residue classes pruned by the Descent Sieve alone at each depth k. Plot the survival curve.
